title: Spec: DTN store-and-forward in spec/07-transport-app.md
description: Add section to spec/07-transport-app.md defining LICHEN's DTN store-and-forward semantics. This is a minimal custody-transfer profile using CoAP semantics, NOT full Bundle Protocol. Reference RFC 9171 (BPv7) and RFC 4838 (DTN Architecture) as conceptual basis for custody transfer and store-and-forward terminology, then explicitly state: LICHEN implements these concepts at the CoAP layer rather than adopting the Bundle Protocol, because BPv7 bundle overhead (~30+ bytes) is prohibitive on 255-byte LoRa frames where SCHC+link security already consume 50-60 bytes. Design: (1) CoAP option DTN-TTL carries absolute expiry time (4 bytes, GNSS wall-clock). (2) Custody transfer = CoAP CON ACK from a relay/gateway-class node; the ACK IS the custody signal — no new protocol. Relay persists message to flash upon ACK; if it cannot persist, it does not ACK and sender retries to different neighbor. (3) DTN store is bounded, TTL-expiring, flash-backed per node class (leaf=none, router=4, relay=256, gateway=4096+). (4) Forward: when route to destination appears (new neighbor, gateway up), drain matching store entries into TX queue. Full BPv7 interop is out of scope — if needed later, a gateway translates BPv7 bundles to/from CoAP DTN messages, same pattern as Yggdrasil gateway.
design: Wire format: single CoAP option (DTN-TTL, option number TBD, 4 bytes, uint32 unix epoch). Custody signal: standard CoAP CON/ACK — no new message types. Store keyed by (destination IPv6, message token). Eviction: TTL expiry first, then LRU within same priority. Custody chain: each custodian is responsible until the next custodian ACKs or TTL expires. Sender stops retransmitting after first custody ACK. References: RFC 9171 (BPv7 concepts), RFC 4838 (DTN architecture), RFC 9172 (BPSec — not adopted, OSCORE covers E2E).
